lowest_kept_note: Ranked by views, then counted sources. Nine kept places show counted_sources 0 in verdicts.json (Woody Island, Peak Charles NP, Beringbooding, Elachbutting, Jilakin, Yorkrakine and Yeerakine rocks, Toolibin Lake, Lake Dumbleyung): each judge reason records a counted source found on re-look (DBCA, Tourism WA, Wheatbelt Tourism or the board), so their real count is at least 1; all have views above 0, so they rank above the twelve listed.

stronger_left_out.name: Lake Hillier
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 1: re-looked: Tourism WA (westernaustralia.com) has an attraction page for it; famous pink lake on Middle Island, 44,580 page views. | Review objection: Rule 2: there is no public landing; it is seen only from a scenic flight or an occasional cruise, so a visitor cannot stand there; COVERAGE allows 'what a scenic flight flies over' as the spot, which argues for keeping, but nothing can be done on site.

stronger_left_out.name: Great Victoria Desert
stronger_left_out.reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 It is a vast desert region with no visitor point; not a spot (rule 2: nothing to do at a place).

stronger_left_out.name: Pink Lake (Esperance)
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Wikivoyage Esperance See listing); the Golden Outback Esperance page does not name it. | Review objection: Wikivoyage itself says it is 'not particularly pink nor lake-like', a salt pan whose colour has gone; visitors expecting a pink lake are disappointed. Case for: well known name (29k views), a roadside look on the edge of town.

stronger_left_out.name: Nullarbor Links
stronger_left_out.reason: COVERAGE 'a spot is a place' / Rule 3: an 18-hole golf course spread over 1,365 km of the Eyre Highway with holes at roadhouses in WA and SA; it is an activity with no single place to pin.

stronger_left_out.name: CY O'Connor Pipeline
stronger_left_out.reason: Not a place: a 530 km water pipeline; it is seen at its stops, chiefly Mount Charlotte Reservoir and Lookout (Wikivoyage Kalgoorlie-Boulder), so as a spot it is a duplicate of that.

stronger_left_out.name: Yalgoo
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 1 + 2, town: the Shire of Yalgoo's tourism pages (fetched) give the town its own attractions. These are the Courthouse Museum (open on call to the Shire, with toilets and an information bay), the Dominican Chapel of St Hyacinth (a Monsignor Hawes chapel, which has its own attraction page), the restored railway station, Jokers Tunnel, a heritage trail, and the Yalgoo Arts and Cultural Centre. It is also the base for the Dalgaranga crater, the wildflower drives and the Gascoyne Murchison Outback Pathways. | Review objection: The only source is the shire's own website: Wikivoyage has no Yalgoo page, the Golden Outback board page returned 404, and Tourism WA's page did not render to a script, so it was not confirmed. The town has about 100 people, and most of its pull is the seasonal wildflowers and the station country beyond it. Its listed draws are small and some open only on request (the courthouse museum is 'call Shire for details'). A town with one source and short stops is marginal. If kept, it is a low-rank gateway, and the Hawes chapel might be the stronger single spot.

stronger_left_out.name: Outback Way
stronger_left_out.reason: COVERAGE 'a spot is a place': a 2,700 km road from Laverton to Winton, mostly in the NT and Queensland; it is a way of travelling, and the places along it are the spots.

stronger_left_out.name: Great Western Woodlands
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 3 / not a place: a 16-million-hectare bioregion with no single visitor point; visitors experience it in the parks that are candidates in their own right (Goldfields Woodlands NP, Boorabbin NP, Burra Rock, Kalgoorlie Arboretum).

stronger_left_out.name: Bunda Cliffs
stronger_left_out.reason: Outside the region: the Bunda Cliffs and their signposted viewing spots run east of Eucla and Border Village, in South Australia (candidate coordinates 131.1 E); they belong to no WA region.

stronger_left_out.name: Dalgaranga Meteorite Crater
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 1 + 3, one counted source: the Shire of Yalgoo's tourism attraction page (fetched) lists it with daylight opening hours, signposting and no facilities on Dalgaranga Station, 100 km north of Yalgoo. It is a distinct natural draw: Australia's smallest well-preserved impact crater (24 m across, 3 m deep) and the only known crater made by a mesosiderite meteorite. It is permanent and open to the public (rules 2 and 4). | Review objection: Only one counted source: no board, Wikivoyage or guidebook page was found. australiasgoldenoutback.com has no page for it, and ExplorOz is a 4WD place directory, not counted. It is a small hollow on a pastoral station about 100 km from town on unsealed station roads, so the visit is a short look of perhaps 15-30 minutes. That is the marginal combination COVERAGE sends to review (one source and a short visit). The case for keeping it is that it is a scientifically unique, quirky stop that a shire signposts for visitors.

stronger_left_out.name: Kellerberrin
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 1: own board page naming a folk museum, Kellerberrin Hill Lookout and Kokerbin Rock nearby. | Review objection: Small Wheatbelt service town on the Great Eastern Highway; its strongest draw (Kokerbin Rock) is 40 km away and would be its own spot; one counted source and no Wikivoyage page; fails the friend test unless passing through.

stronger_left_out.name: Mundrabilla meteorite
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 3: the meteorite is not there (the masses are in museums); what the visitor finds is the Mundrabilla roadhouse with a small museum, which is a business, and one counted source.

stronger_left_out.name: Lake Lefroy

stronger_left_out.name: Lake Carnegie

stronger_left_out_note: Every review or reject candidate whose score (views, then counted sources) beats the lowest-scoring kept place (views 0, 1 counted source). Each carries the judge's concrete 'What qualifies' reason and, for review, the skeptic's objection. Review entries are the owner's decision (placement.json -> review). The highest-scoring are Lake Hillier (review: no public landing, seen only from the air or an occasional cruise), Great Victoria Desert (reject: no counted source, no visitor point), Pink Lake (review: one source, no longer pink), Nullarbor Links (reject: a golf course strung over 1,365 km, not one place) and CY O'Connor Pipeline (reject: a pipeline seen at its stops, chiefly Mount Charlotte, which is kept).
strongest_outsiders_note: Candidates of any verdict outside every proposed destination's span (75% of defaultZoomSpanKm), by views; kept ones are placed as standalone spots (placed_as).

benchmark.applies: The NZ benchmark in COVERAGE step 6 cannot be run on a WA region; region checks instead.
checks: Lucky Bay, Hellfire Bay, Frenchman Peak: spots of Cape Le Grand National Park (pass).
Wave Rock: headline spot of Hyden (pass). Super Pit Lookout: headline spot of Kalgoorlie-Boulder (pass).
Lake Ballard (Antony Gormley's Inside Australia): standalone, not under a town 51 km away (pass).

A spot is a place, not the vehicle: Woody Island is the spot, not the boat tour (Woody Island Eco Tours); Nullarbor Links, Outback Way, Golden Quest Discovery Trail, Golden Pipeline Heritage Trail, Pathways to Wave Rock, PUBLIC Silo Art Trail and Wheatbelt Way rejected as routes, while each silo is its own spot (pass).

Long feature at its access point: 90 Mile Straight pinned at its sign near Caiguna, not its midpoint; Canning Stock Route placed once at the midpoint of the whole route per the run-wide decision (pass).
Town wrappers: Leonora, Kambalda and Dundas merged into their one attraction; Hyden, Esperance, Kalgoorlie-Boulder, Merredin and Ravensthorpe are destinations, not spots (pass).

National parks: Cape Le Grand (8 spots) is a destination; Cape Arid, Stokes, Goldfields Woodlands, Goongarrie, Peak Charles and Dryandra Woodland have fewer than four kept spots and stand alone; no park is a spot of another park (pass). Eucla National Park is a spot of the Nullarbor Plain region, not of a park.

Gateway villages whose draw is the journey beyond go to review, not keep: Yalgoo and the Dalgaranga crater are review per the brief; Laverton and Wiluna were kept by the judges as towns with draws of their own (heritage, museum, police station complex / heritage walks, statue).

Negative benchmarks: no once-a-week market, festival, civic building or minor memorial is placed (Boulder Town Hall, Menzies Town Hall, Kambalda Pioneer Cemetery, Traveller's Cross and Eyre Memorial are review or reject).
